claims.evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Binding of NONO, SFPQ, RBM14 and PSPC1 on Neat1 RNA displayed a rhythmic pattern in GH4C1 cells.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 3C, binding of the four paraspeckle-associated proteins on Neat1 RNA displayed a rhythmic pattern (cosinor fit values given in Figure 3—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RIP experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Maximum binding of the four paraspeckle proteins on Neat1 RNA was reached between 6 and 10 hr after the medium change.
claims.source: Maximum binding on Neat1 RNA was reached between 6 and 10 hr after the medium change for the four proteins (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the RIP data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The total number of paraspeckles per well fluctuated over time, being significantly lower 15 hr after the medium change.
claims.source: In cells arrested at four different times after the medium change, the total number of paraspeckles per well was shown to fluctuate, being significantly lower 15 hr after the medium change i.e. at a time when Neat1 RNA levels were around the lowest levels (Figure 3D, F3,103=9.531 p<0.0001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative FISH data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: The mean number of paraspeckles per cell reached a minimum value 15 hr after the medium change.
claims.source: Furthermore at this time point, the mean number of paraspeckles per cell reached a minimum value (Figure 3D, F3447= 5.456, p<0.001).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative FISH data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: The rhythm of Neat1 and its associated proteins translates into a rhythm in the number of paraspeckles inside the cells.
claims.source: Taken together, these results showed that the rhythm of Neat1 and its associated proteins reported above translate into a rhythm in the number of paraspeckles inside the cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of rhythmic Neat1 expression and rhythmic paraspeckle number.

claims.claim: IRAlu elements derived from NICN1 significantly reduced EGFP expression when compared with the Alu element.
claims.source: In agreement with previous results by Chen et al (Chen and Carmichael, 2008), the IRAlu elements derived from NICN1 significantly reduced EGFP expression when compared with the Alu element (Figure 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claims.claim: IRAlu elements caused a significant reduction in the number of fluorescent cells compared to Alu element.
claims.source: This is here evidenced both by the significant reduction in the number of fluorescent cells (Figure 4B) and by the significant decrease in relative EGFP levels measured by western blotting in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to both Alu–egfp cell line (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: IRAlu elements caused a significant decrease in relative EGFP levels measured by western blotting in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to Alu-egfp cell line.
claims.source: This is here evidenced both by the significant reduction in the number of fluorescent cells (Figure 4B) and by the significant decrease in relative EGFP levels measured by western blotting in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to both Alu–egfp cell line (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: No difference in gene expression was observed between the parent plasmid pEGFP and derivatives that contained a single Alu element.
claims.source: By contrast, we have not observed any difference in gene expression between the parent plasmid pEGFP and derivatives that contained a single Alu element (data not shown).
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments, though data is not shown.

claims.claim: IRAlu from Nicn1 caused a more than two-fold greater nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA when compared with the corresponding Alu element.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4D, the IRAlu from Nicn1 caused a more than two-fold greater nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA when compared with the corresponding Alu element.
claims.evidence: This is supported by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: There is no significant difference in nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution of egfp-Alu mRNA compared with control.
claims.source: On the other hand, there is no significant difference in nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution of egfp-Alu mRNA compared with control (data not shown), consistent with our finding that a single Alu element in the 3'-UTR does not affect EGFP gene expression.
claims.evidence: This is stated as an observation, though data is not shown.

claims.claim: Nuclear retention of IRAlu-containing egfp mRNA correlates with silencing of EGFP protein expression.
claims.source: It then appears that nuclear retention of IRAlu-containing egfp mRNA correlates with silencing of EGFP protein expression (Figure 4A–C).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between nuclear retention data and protein expression data.

claims.claim: PSPC1 protein was associated with IRAlu-egfp mRNA but not with Alu-egfp mRNA.
claims.source: While the enrichment in lncRNA Neat1 obtained after use of PSPC1 antibody was comparable in the two cell lines (Figure 4E), enrichment in egfp mRNA was significant only in IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 4F), attesting that PSPC1 protein was associated to IRAlu-egfp and not to Alu-egfp mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RIP experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: The enrichment in lncRNA Neat1 obtained after use of PSPC1 antibody was comparable in Alu-egfp and IRAlu-egfp cell lines.
claims.source: While the enrichment in lncRNA Neat1 obtained after use of PSPC1 antibody was comparable in the two cell lines (Figure 4E), enrichment in egfp mRNA was significant only in IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 4F), attesting that PSPC1 protein was associated to IRAlu-egfp and not to Alu-egfp mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is supported by RIP experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Two anti-sense oligonucleotides allowed a 30 to 40-fold enrichment in Neat1 RNA compared to Neat1 RNA input from cross-linked GH4C1 cellular extracts.
claims.source: With this strategy, we found that two anti-sense oligonucleotides allowed a 30 to 40-fold enrichment in Neat1 RNA compared to Neat1 RNA input from cross-linked GH4C1 cellular extracts (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The enrichment in Neat1 was not statistically different in Alu-egfp and IRAlu-egfp cell lines after Neat1 RNA pull-down.
claims.source: While one of the specific oligonucleotide (S oligo 2) is more efficient than the other (S oligo 1) to pull-down Neat1, the enrichment in Neat1 was not statistically different in the two Alu-egfp and IRAlu-egfp cell lines (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: The amounts of egfp mRNA retrieved after Neat1 RNA pull-down were significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp compared to Alu-egfp cell line.
claims.source: By contrast, the amounts of egfp mRNA retrieved after Neat1 RNA pull-down by the two specific probes compared to the non-specific probe were significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp compared to Alu-egfp cell line (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: IRAlu-egfp mRNA was preferentially associated with Neat1-containing paraspeckles compared to Alu-egfp mRNA.
claims.source: This result clearly showed that IRAlu-egfp mRNA was preferentially associated with Neat1-containing paraspeckles compared to Alu-egfp mRNA.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the RNA pull-down data showing higher enrichment of IRAlu-egfp mRNA with Neat1.

claims.claim: High amplitude circadian variations in the nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio of egfp mRNA were observed in IRAlu-egfp cell line.
claims.source: We showed that in addition to the previously described higher ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic egfp mRNA in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to Alu-egfp cell lines (Figure 4D) we also found high amplitude circadian variations in this ratio in IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by time-course nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: The magnitude of the rhythmic pattern of nuclear/cytoplasmic egfp mRNA ratio was highly reduced in Alu-egfp cell line compared to IRAlu-egfp cell line.
claims.source: Whereas it was observed that the nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio of egfp mRNA could also be fitted by a cosinor equation in Alu-egfp cell line, the magnitude of this rhythmic pattern was highly reduced (Figure 5A) as compared to IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of cosinor fit parameters shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—source data 1.

claims.claim: Neat1 RNA levels were reduced to around 60% after treatment with specific siRNA compared to negative control siRNA in IRAlu-egfp cell line.
claims.source: Neat1 has been previously shown by others to be effectively knocked down by siRNA (Chen and Carmichael, 2009; Clemson et al., 2009), and we indeed verified by RT-qPCR that Neat1 RNA levels were reduced in IRAlu-egfp cell line to around 60% after treatment with specific siRNA compared to negative control siRNA, a decrease that was comparable to that obtained with Neat1 ASO (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A)
claims.evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Neat1 rhythmic expression pattern was suppressed by both Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO.
claims.source: more importantly, whereas Neat1 rhythmic expression pattern was not affected by negative control (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), it was suppressed both by Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by time-course RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: The relative ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic egfp mRNA levels was significantly decreased when IRAlu-egfp cells were transfected with Neat1 siRNA or Neat1 ASO compared to negative control.
claims.source: In addition, when IRAlu-egfp cells were transfected either by Neat1 siRNA or Neat1 ASO as compared to negative control, the relative ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic egfp mRNA levels was significantly decreased (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Circadian egfp mRNA nuclear retention was abolished after both Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO transfection.
claims.source: Moreover, whereas the circadian egfp mRNA nuclear retention was not affected after transfection of the cells by the negative control (not shown), it was abolished after both Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO transfection (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by time-course data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: The IRAlu-egfp reporter does not cycle when paraspeckles are disrupted.
claims.source: These loss of function experiments showed that the IRAlu-egfp reporter does not cycle when paraspeckles are disrupted.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the loss of rhythmic nuclear retention after Neat1 knockdown.

claims.claim: The percent of cells that could be fitted by cosinor equation with a R2>0.5 was significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to the Alu-egfp and egfp cell lines.
claims.source: The percent of cells that could be fitted by cosinor equation with a R2>0.5 was then calculated for each cell line. This percent was significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to the Alu-egfp and egfp cell lines (Figure 5D) allowing to show that insertion of an IRAlu element in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA promoted EGFP protein circadian expression.
claims.evidence: This is supported by real-time video microscopy data shown in Figure 5D.

claims.claim: Insertion of an IRAlu element in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA promoted EGFP protein circadian expression.
claims.source: This percent was significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to the Alu-egfp and egfp cell lines (Figure 5D) allowing to show that insertion of an IRAlu element in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA promoted EGFP protein circadian expression.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the higher percentage of rhythmic cells in IRAlu-egfp cell line.

claims.claim: 4268 genes (28% of expressed transcripts in GH4C1 cells) were common to the lists obtained with the two specific oligonucleotides used for Neat1 RNA pull-down.
claims.source: We assessed the specificity of Neat 1 RNA pull-down by crossing the FPKM>1-limited lists obtained with the two specific oligonucleotides. 4268 genes (28% of expressed transcripts in GH4C1 cells) were common to the two lists (Figure 6—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data analysis.

claims.claim: The 4268 common genes represented 65% of the list obtained with S oligo 1 and 83% of the list obtained with S oligo 2.
claims.source: This represented 65% of the list obtained with S oligo 1 and 83% of the list obtained with S oligo 2.
claims.evidence: This is calculated from the RNA sequencing data.

claims.claim: 68 genes out of 362 from the list of pituitary circadian transcripts (18.8%) were found to be included in the Neat1 RNA targets dataset.
claims.source: We first compared the mouse pituitary circadian transcriptome previously published (Hughes et al., 2007) with our data set of Neat1 RNA targets. It appeared that 68 genes out of 362 from the list of pituitary circadian transcripts (18.8% ) were found to be included in our data set (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of datasets shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: 182 genes out of 675 from the list of post-transcriptional circadian genes in the liver (27%) were found to be included in the Neat1 RNA targets dataset.
claims.source: To this end, we compared the list of putative post-transcriptional cycling transcripts established by Menet et al. (Menet et al., 2012) in the mouse liver with our list of Neat1 RNA targets. Although these two lists have been established in two different tissues from two different species, it appeared that 182 genes out of 675 from the list of post-transcriptional circadian genes in the liver (27%) were found to be included in our data set (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of datasets shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Very few genes (24 genes) were common to the list of Hughes et al. and that of Menet et al.
claims.source: In agreement with the assumption that rhythmic circadian genes are tissue specific, we found very few genes (24 genes) common to the list of Hughes et al. (<7%) (Hughes et al., 2007) and that of Menet et al. (<4%) (Menet et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of the two published datasets.

claims.claim: 6 genes out of 24 common genes (25%) between Hughes et al. and Menet et al. lists were Neat1 RNA targets.
claims.source: In spite of this reduced overlap, we found that 6 genes out of these 24 common genes (25% ) were Neat1 RNA targets (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison of datasets shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Seven selected genes (Calr, Evi5, Maged1, Canx, Pcbp2, Syne1, and Fkbp4) were significantly enriched after Neat1 RNA pull-down by the two specific probes compared to the non-specific probe.
claims.source: First we verified by qPCR the specific association of the seven selected genes with Neat1. To this end, we determined the enrichment in these seven mRNA obtained after Neat1 RNA pull-down with the two specific biotinylated complementary oligonucleotides that target Neat1 compared to the biotinylated irrelevant probe. As shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1, the seven selected genes were significantly enriched after Neat1 RNA pull-down by the two specific probes compared to the non-specific probe.
claims.evidence: This is supported by qPCR validation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Seven selected genes displayed a rhythmic pattern of nuclear retention in IRAlu-egfp cells.
claims.source: We further found that the seven selected genes displayed a rhythmic pattern of nuclear retention in IRAlu-egfp cells since values obtained for their relative mRNA ratio between nucleoplasm and cytoplasm over the time can be fitted by a sine wave curve with a R squared >0.55 (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2, Figure 6—source data 2).
claims.evidence: This is supported by time-course nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: The minimum value of the relative ratio nuclear/cytoplasmic mRNA of the seven selected genes occurred roughly 20 hr after the medium change.
claims.source: It may be noticed that the minimum value of the relative ratio nuclear / cytoplasmic mRNA occurred roughly 20 hr after the medium change, i.e. at a time when the levels of paraspeckle protein components and Neat1 RNA were the lowest (Figure 3).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the time-course data and correlated with paraspeckle component levels.

claims.claim: Knockdown of Neat1 RNA by Neat1 siRNA or Neat1 ASO disrupted the circadian pattern of the ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic levels of the seven selected mRNA.
claims.source: In Figure 6C–D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2, it was shown that knockdown of Neat1 RNA, either by Neat1 siRNA (Figure 6C) or by Neat1 ASO (Figure 6D) disrupted the circadian pattern of the ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic levels of the seven selected mRNA as assessed by the inability to fit the values obtained with a sine wave curve with a R squared >0.55.
claims.evidence: This is supported by loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 6C-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Paraspeckles play a role in the rhythmic expression of the seven selected genes.
claims.source: These results showed that paraspeckles play a role in the rhythmic expression of theses selected genes.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the loss of rhythmic nuclear retention after paraspeckle disruption.

claims.claim: Paraspeckles are found in almost all cultured cell lines and primary cultures from tissues, except for embryonic stem cells.
claims.source: Paraspeckles are found in almost all of the cultured cell lines and primary cultures from tissues (Bond and Fox, 2009), except for embryonic stem cells (Chen and Carmichael, 2009).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claims.claim: Four RNA-binding proteins (NONO, PSPC1, SFPQ, and RBM14) are classified as 'classical' paraspeckle protein components.
claims.source: Four RNA-binding proteins, including three members of the Drosophila melanogaster behavior human splicing (DBHS) family proteins (NONO, PSPC1 and SFPQ) and RNA-binding motif protein 14 (RBM14) are classified as 'classical' paraspeckle protein components (Bond and Fox, 2009; Prasanth et al., 2005; Fox et al., 2002; Nakagawa and Hirose, 2012).
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claims.claim: Both endogenous and tagged forms of paraspeckle proteins are found localized within the nucleoplasm as well as paraspeckles in mammalian cells.
claims.source: Both endogenous and tagged forms of these proteins are found localized within the nucleoplasm as well as paraspeckles in mammalian cells.
claims.evidence: This is established knowledge about paraspeckle protein localization.

claims.claim: All four paraspeckle protein components are distributed both in the nucleoplasm and in subnuclear foci in rat pituitary cell line.
claims.source: With a confocal fluorescent study, we report in a rat pituitary cell line that all four paraspeckle protein components are distributed both in the nucleoplasm and in subnuclear foci.
claims.evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: Paraspeckles are small, irregularly sized and unevenly distributed subnuclear bodies in rat pituitary cell nuclei.
claims.source: This allows not only to provide evidence for the existence of paraspeckles in rat pituitary cell nuclei but also to show that as already reported in other cell types, paraspeckles are small, irregularly sized and unevenly distributed subnuclear bodies.
claims.evidence: This is observed from immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1.

claims.claim: When identified by a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and confocal microscopy, paraspeckles appear as round foci in rat pituitary cells.
claims.source: Confirming previous reports in other cell types, when identified by a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and confocal microscopy, paraspeckles appear as round foci in rat pituitary cells.
claims.evidence: This is supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: The diameter of round paraspeckle foci is in the range of around 360 nm.
claims.source: The diameter of such round foci is in the range of that estimated in previous studies (around 360 nm).
claims.evidence: This is compared with previous literature estimates.

claims.claim: After use of a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and STORM analysis, paraspeckles appear as oblong structures with smaller dimensions reminiscent of the interchromatin granule-associated zone (IGAZ).
claims.source: However after use of a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and STORM analysis, paraspeckles appear more likely as oblong structures with smaller dimensions reminiscent of the interchromatin granule-associated zone (IGAZ) that had been observed under electron microscope and had been reported to correspond to paraspeckles (Cardinale et al., 2007; Bond and Fox, 2009; Souquere et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is supported by STORM data shown in Figure 2C and compared with previous literature.

claims.claim: Width and height measurements obtained after STORM analysis of Neat1 RNA FISH staining are smaller than the dimensions of IGAZ nuclear bodies established by electron microscopy analysis in human and mouse cells.
claims.source: Width and height measurements obtained after STORM analysis of Neat1 RNA FISH staining are smaller than the dimensions of IGAZ nuclear bodies established by an electron microscopy analysis in human and mouse cells (Souquere et al., 2010) suggesting that either IGAZ/paraspeckle nuclear bodies are smaller in rat than in mouse cells or alternatively and more likely, Neat1 RNA staining does not fill in all the nuclear bodies as already proposed (Souquere et al., 2010).

claims.claim: The circadian expression pattern of Neat1 RNA in several mouse tissues reflects variations in paraspeckle number.
claims.source: It may then be assumed that the circadian expression pattern of Neat1 RNA described here in a number of mouse tissue also reflects variations in paraspeckle number although it cannot be excluded that paraspeckle size could also oscillate over the circadian period both in pituitary cells and in other oscillators.

claims.claim: IRAlus-containing egfp mRNA appear to be preferentially retained in the nucleus in comparison with those having a single Alu element.
claims.source: As previously reported by Chen and Carmichael (Chen et al., 2008), we found that a pair of IRAlus in the 3'-UTR of egfp can strongly silence EGFP expression in GH4C1 pituitary cell line and after fractionating cytoplasmic and nuclear RNAs from our two cell lines, we observed that IRAlus-containing egfp mRNA appear to be preferentially retained in the nucleus in comparison with those having a single Alu element.

claims.source: This is not the case for HNRNPU and STAUFEN 1 (STAU1)-mediated messenger RNA decay we did not find to display a circadian expression pattern in GH4C1 cells (Guillaumond et al., 2011) and (data not shown) and are then unlikely involved in circadian EGFP expression in Alu-egfp cell line.

claims.claim: The mechanism involved in the circadian nuclear retention of Alu-containing egfp mRNA remains to be determined.
claims.source: The mechanism involved in the circadian nuclear retention of Alu-containing egfp mRNA remains anyway to be determined.
claims.evidence: This acknowledges that the mechanism is not yet understood.

claims.source: Nuclear retention of egfp mRNA in IRAlu-egfp cells is no more cycling when paraspeckles were disrupted assuming that the nuclear retention of the reporter gene by paraspeckles contributes to cycling.

claims.source: Furthermore, on a few circadian genes common to either of these lists or both, we showed a loss of rhythmic pattern when paraspeckles were disrupted assuming that paraspeckle retention plays a relevant role in circadian gene expression.

claims.source: GH4C1 cells, a rat pituitary somatolactotroph line, were obtained in 2012 from ATCC (CCL-82.2, lot number: 58945448, Molsheim, France) with certificate analysis and were confirmed to be free of mycoplasma (MycoAlert, Lonza, Levallois-Perret, France).

results.result: Paraspeckles are present in GH4C1 rat pituitary cells, as demonstrated by immunofluorescence showing nuclear localization of four protein components (SFPQ, NONO, PSPC1, RBM14) with overlapping punctate clusters, and by RIP experiments showing 20-80-fold enrichment of Neat1 RNA with these proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C31-C34 provide converging evidence from immunofluorescence microscopy (C31, C32) and biochemical RIP experiments (C33, C34) that establish the presence of functional paraspeckles in GH4C1 cells. The data are internally consistent and use complementary methodologies.

results.result: Neat1 RNA visualized by FISH appears as nuclear punctates that are elliptical rather than round when analyzed by super-resolution STORM microscopy, with a mean height-to-width ratio of 1.53±0.1 and mean surface area of 24,960±4831 nm².
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C39 describe FISH and STORM microscopy characterization of paraspeckle morphology. The progression from confocal to super-resolution imaging is logical, and quantitative measurements (C38, C39) are provided with appropriate statistics (n=10). The elliptical shape finding (C37) is novel and well-supported by the quantitative ratio.

results.result: All paraspeckle components (proteins RBM14, PSPC1, NONO, SFPQ and Neat1 RNA) display circadian rhythmic expression patterns in GH4C1 cells and in multiple mouse tissues including pituitary, spleen, adrenal gland, and suprachiasmatic nuclei, with rhythmic binding of proteins to Neat1 RNA peaking at 6-10 hours after medium change.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C46 demonstrate circadian rhythmicity using multiple approaches: Western blot for proteins (C40, C41), RT-qPCR for RNA (C42-C44), and RIP for protein-RNA binding (C45, C46). All data were fitted with cosinor equations with R²>0.55, providing statistical support. The consistency across multiple tissues (C43, C44) strengthens the finding.

results.result: The number of paraspeckles per well and per cell fluctuates over time with circadian rhythmicity, reaching minimum values 15 hours after medium change when Neat1 RNA levels are lowest, demonstrating that rhythmic expression of paraspeckle components translates into rhythmic paraspeckle number.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C49 provide quantitative FISH data showing temporal fluctuations in paraspeckle number with statistical significance (p<0.0001 and p<0.001). The correlation between paraspeckle number and Neat1 RNA levels (C49) is a logical inference supported by the temporal correspondence noted in C47.

results.result: IRAlu elements from NICN1 inserted in the 3'-UTR of EGFP significantly reduce EGFP protein expression compared to single Alu elements, causing >2-fold greater nuclear retention of egfp mRNA, and this nuclear retention correlates with silencing of EGFP protein expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C52, C54, C56 demonstrate the functional effect of IRAlu elements using multiple readouts: fluorescence microscopy (C50, C51), Western blot (C52), and nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation (C54). The correlation between nuclear retention and reduced protein expression (C56) is well-supported by the data, though the claim acknowledges this is correlative.

results.result: IRAlu-egfp mRNA is preferentially associated with paraspeckle components compared to Alu-egfp mRNA, as demonstrated by RIP showing PSPC1 association only with IRAlu-egfp and by Neat1 RNA pull-down showing significantly higher enrichment of IRAlu-egfp mRNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C62 use two complementary approaches (RIP and RNA pull-down) to demonstrate specific association of IRAlu-containing mRNA with paraspeckles. The controls are appropriate (C58, C60 show comparable Neat1 enrichment in both cell lines), and the differential enrichment of egfp mRNA (C57, C61) provides strong evidence for the conclusion (C62).

results.result: IRAlu elements in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA induce high-amplitude circadian variations in nuclear/cytoplasmic mRNA ratio, while single Alu elements produce only weak circadian effects with highly reduced magnitude.
results.evaluation: Claims C63, C64, and C6 demonstrate differential circadian effects of IRAlu vs. Alu elements using time-course nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation. The data are fitted with cosinor equations (R²=0.68 for IRAlu, R²=0.73 for Alu), and the comparison of amplitudes is appropriate. The weak effect of single Alu (C6, C64) serves as an important control.

results.result: Disruption of paraspeckles by Neat1 knockdown (siRNA or ASO reducing Neat1 to ~60% of control) abolishes both the rhythmic expression pattern of Neat1 and the circadian nuclear retention of IRAlu-egfp mRNA, demonstrating that paraspeckles are required for circadian cycling of the IRAlu-egfp reporter.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C69 provide loss-of-function evidence using two independent knockdown methods (siRNA and ASO). The knockdown efficiency is validated (C65), the effect on Neat1 rhythmicity is shown (C66), and the functional consequences on egfp mRNA retention are demonstrated (C67, C68). The conclusion (C69) is well-supported by these data.

results.result: IRAlu elements in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA promote circadian EGFP protein expression, as demonstrated by real-time video microscopy showing a significantly higher percentage of cells with rhythmic EGFP fluorescence (R²>0.5) in IRAlu-egfp cells compared to Alu-egfp and control egfp cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C70, C71, and C7 use real-time video microscopy to demonstrate circadian protein expression. The statistical approach (percentage of cells fitting cosinor with R²>0.5) is appropriate, and the comparison across three cell lines provides good controls. This represents the functional endpoint of the nuclear retention mechanism.

results.result: RNA sequencing of Neat1 pull-down identified 4268 genes as paraspeckle-associated targets in GH4C1 cells, with significant overlap with published circadian transcriptomes: 18.8% overlap with pituitary circadian genes and 27% overlap with liver post-transcriptional circadian genes, including 25% of genes common to both published datasets.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C77 describe RNA-seq analysis with appropriate validation (two specific oligonucleotides with 65-83% overlap, C72-C73). The cross-species and cross-tissue comparisons (C74-C77) are acknowledged as limitations but show meaningful overlaps. The enrichment of circadian genes among paraspeckle targets supports the biological relevance of the findings.

results.result: Seven selected genes (Calr, Evi5, Maged1, Canx, Pcbp2, Syne1, Fkbp4) identified as Neat1 RNA targets by pull-down and validated by qPCR display rhythmic nuclear retention patterns in IRAlu-egfp cells (R²>0.55), with minimum nuclear/cytoplasmic ratios occurring ~20 hours after medium change when paraspeckle components are lowest.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C80 provide validation of RNA-seq findings using qPCR (C78) and demonstrate functional rhythmic nuclear retention for selected endogenous genes (C79). The temporal correlation with paraspeckle component levels (C80) strengthens the mechanistic link. The R²>0.55 threshold is consistently applied.

results.result: Knockdown of Neat1 RNA by siRNA or ASO disrupts the circadian pattern of nuclear/cytoplasmic ratios for seven selected endogenous genes, demonstrating that paraspeckles play a role in the rhythmic expression of these genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C82 provide loss-of-function evidence for endogenous genes using the same knockdown approaches validated earlier. The disruption of rhythmic patterns (inability to fit with R²>0.55) after paraspeckle disruption supports the mechanistic role. This extends the findings from the reporter system to endogenous genes.

results.result: Paraspeckles control circadian gene expression at a post-transcriptional level through their circadian expression, with nuclear retention by paraspeckles contributing to the cycling of both reporter genes and endogenous circadian genes, suggesting that circadian mRNA oscillations can be post-transcriptionally controlled through rhythmic nuclear retention by paraspeckle nuclear bodies.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C8, C105, C106, and C108 represent the main conclusions of the study. These are well-supported by the collective evidence from multiple experimental approaches: demonstration of circadian paraspeckle expression, IRAlu-mediated circadian nuclear retention, loss-of-function experiments, and validation with endogenous genes. The conclusion is appropriately cautious ("can be" rather than "are").

results.result: Single Alu elements in the 3'-UTR do not significantly affect EGFP gene expression or nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution of egfp mRNA compared to control.
results.evaluation: Claims C53 and C55 state that single Alu elements have no effect, but both explicitly note that data are not shown. While this is consistent with the weak circadian effect observed (C6, C64), the absence of presented data makes these specific claims uncertain. This represents a minor control that would strengthen the manuscript if included.

results.result: STORM analysis reveals that paraspeckles appear as oblong structures with dimensions smaller than previously reported IGAZ nuclear bodies, suggesting either species differences or that Neat1 RNA staining does not fill the entire nuclear body.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C91 compare STORM measurements with published electron microscopy data. The observation is well-documented (C90), and the interpretation (C91) appropriately acknowledges alternative explanations. This represents a technical advance in paraspeckle visualization but is secondary to the main findings.

results.result: The circadian expression pattern of Neat1 RNA in mouse tissues may reflect variations in paraspeckle number, though oscillations in paraspeckle size cannot be excluded.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C93 are explicitly speculative ("may be assumed," "cannot be excluded"). While the inference is reasonable based on the GH4C1 cell data showing correlation between Neat1 levels and paraspeckle number, direct evidence in tissues is not provided. This represents a reasonable extrapolation but requires validation.

results.result: The weak circadian EGFP expression in Alu-egfp cells may be explained by rhythmic expression of RNA-binding proteins that target antisense Alu elements, such as HNRNPC which displays circadian expression in pituitary, though the mechanism remains to be determined.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C104 are explicitly speculative ("may be speculated," "remains to be determined"). While HNRNPC is identified as a candidate (C101), and HNRNPU/STAU1 are ruled out (C102-C103), no direct experimental evidence links any specific factor to the weak Alu effect. This represents reasonable speculation but lacks experimental support.

results.result: Background knowledge claims about paraspeckles, circadian biology, Alu elements, and prior work are established in the literature.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1-C2, C9-C30, C83-C85, C97-C98, C107) represent established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations. They provide context for the current work and are not novel findings of this study. The citations appear appropriate and the knowledge claims are consistent with the field.

results.result: Paraspeckles in GH4C1 rat pituitary cells are distributed in both nucleoplasm and subnuclear foci, appearing as small, irregularly sized, unevenly distributed bodies that appear round under confocal microscopy with diameter ~360 nm.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C89 describe basic characterization of paraspeckles in the cell line used. The observations are supported by immunofluorescence and FISH data (C86-C88), and the size estimate (C89) is consistent with literature. This represents standard characterization necessary for the study.

results.result: IRAlu elements in the 3'-UTR of egfp strongly silence EGFP expression through preferential nuclear retention of the mRNA, with association of IRAlu-egfp mRNA with Neat1 providing evidence for nuclear retention by paraspeckles.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C96, C99 summarize the basic IRAlu effect and its mechanism. These are well-supported by the experimental data (Figures 4-5) and represent confirmation/extension of prior work by Chen and Carmichael (2008) in a new cell type. The Neat1 pull-down (C99) provides stronger evidence than previous RIP alone.

results.result: GH4C1 cells were obtained from ATCC in 2012 with certificate of analysis and confirmed mycoplasma-free.
results.evaluation: Claim C109 provides cell line authentication information. This is good practice for reproducibility but represents methodological documentation rather than a scientific finding. The information is clearly stated and verifiable.
